SMTO-GWT-0008 — SMTO couldn't load the saved identity it uses with Gateways

GUID: 89b96b8b-50ed-48e6-ae6a-142888bd43cb
Slug: controller-identity-unavailable
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • Your Gateways recognize SMTO by a security key saved on this computer. SMTO couldn't read that key, so it didn't send this request and can't use your Gateways until the key is back.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure SMTO is started by the same user account on this computer as before, not by a different user or an administrator account. The key is saved in that user's personal folder, so another account can't see it.
  2. If SMTO was moved to a new computer or restored from a backup, ask the person who installed it to restore the old identity folder too. The Gateways trust that exact key and won't accept a new one on their own.
  3. Check that this computer's disk isn't full and that SMTO can save files in its user folder. SMTO also has to save small records each time it links to a Gateway.
  4. If the key is truly lost, ask the manager of each Gateway to reset its pairing on that computer. A reset is the only safe way for a Gateway to trust a new SMTO key.

What success looks like

  • In Settings › Setup › Gateways, Check connection shows Connected and tasks run on the Gateway again.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's identity folder to make it start fresh; every Gateway would then reject it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server's controller identity (RSA signing key or a saved Gateway pairing receipt) could not be read, validated or saved; an initialized identity with a missing key is rejected rather than silently replaced.

What this means

  • The controller's stored RSA identity or pairing marker could not be read, validated or persisted. An initialized identity with a missing key is rejected instead of silently creating a replacement. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The controller's stored RSA identity or pairing marker could not be read, validated or persisted. An initialized identity with a missing key is rejected instead of silently creating a replacement.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the configured controller identity directory and permissions, retained initialization marker and available backup without exposing private key bytes.

How to fix it

  • Check the identity directory (SMTO_CONTROLLER_STATE_DIR, else ~/.smto/controller/identity, or %LOCALAPPDATA%\SMTO\Controller\identity on Windows): identity-key.pem must be a readable 2048-bit RSA key owned by the Server's OS user, and gateways/<fingerprint>.json receipts must be readable. Restore the original key from backup and fix ownership or disk space; replacing the identity deliberately requires re-pairing every Gateway with its local reset command.
  • Restore the controller identity and supported state storage. Do not silently replace trusted identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The controller loads its original valid identity and authenticates to its existing paired Gateway.

What not to do

  • Do not automatically trust a replacement identity or disable certificate verification.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
